findings.location: crosswalk.json papers[1] (VeriHarness 2610.00972).grounding.claims[8] (n 9); papers[3] (JAZ) claims[5]; papers[7] (MASS) claims[4].statusDetail; README seed table 'Availability (V / NF)' column
findings.finding: The round-2 rewrite of VeriHarness check 9 changed its meaning. The text went from 'A released rollout corpus and code; licence if stated.' to 'A released rollout corpus and code, and their licence.', and the status is still VERIFIED with no statusDetail. The paper states no licence for either release: the record's own codeAvailability says 'Licence: not stated in the paper for either release', pp. 1 and 22 contain no licence text, and the only licence on p. 21 is the MIT licence of a runtime dependency. So the public record now reads as if VeriHarness's licence was verified. JAZ check 6 ('Code availability and licence.') is VERIFIED too, but its statusDetail ('VERIFIED (availability) / NOT_FOUND (licence)') discloses the split. Because each check combines code availability with the licence, the AVAILABILITY_CHECK tally of 4 verified / 6 not found hides that none of the eight seed papers states a licence. Smaller point: MASS claim 5's statusDetail still refers to the 'average improvement' that the removed instruction asked for.
findings.requiredChange: Separate code and data availability from the licence statement, either as a separate LICENCE_CHECK kind or as two checks per paper, so the tally shows 0 of 8 papers stating a licence. At minimum, reword VeriHarness check 9 (for example 'A released rollout corpus and code; licence not stated'), give it a statusDetail matching JAZ check 6, and say in the README that the availability column counts code and data, not licences. Reword the MASS claim 5 statusDetail to match the cleaned claim. Update SEED_CLAIMS if the counts change.

findings.location: crosswalk.json definitions.reuseModes.LICENSE_BLOCKED (copied from roadmap research.reuseModes); README Definitions table
findings.finding: The new reuse-mode vocabulary contradicts four records. LICENSE_BLOCKED is defined as 'No OSI licence, no licence file or NOASSERTION at check time', but four repositories that fit that definition carry a different mode: langfuse (NOASSERTION, PLANNED_BASELINE), ai-boost/awesome-harness-engineering and EvoMap/awesome-agent-evolution (NOASSERTION, INDEX_ONLY), and claudes-c-compiler (CC0-1.0, which is not an OSI licence, REFERENCE_DESIGN). The checker's REUSE_OUTCOMES table encodes the real rule: the reuse mode records the intended use, the policy outcome bounds it, and licenceCeiling is binding. The definition text does not say that, so a reader applying it would classify these four records differently.
findings.requiredChange: Add a precedence sentence to the definitions. For example: LICENSE_BLOCKED applies when no other mode applies; PLANNED_BASELINE, INDEX_ONLY, and REFERENCE_DESIGN for open content keep their mode; licenceCeiling decides what is allowed. Alternatively, reword the LICENSE_BLOCKED text in the record. The roadmap text can stay as it is.

findings.location: scripts/research_adoption_v2.py (HYGIENE, PROMPT_RESIDUE, PLANNED_BASELINE mention, ceiling()); builder roadmapCheck normalisation; SEED_STATUS for VeriHarness
findings.finding:
Residual limits after round 2. None affects the current data.
(a) The obfuscated e-mail pattern only matches .com/.org/.net/.edu: the probe accepted '<user> at <host>.ac.uk' and '<user> at <host>.co'.
(b) The home-path rule does not match '~/'.
(c) Bare personal names cannot be caught by a pattern; the builder's SCRUB list and review carry that.
(d) PROMPT_RESIDUE is a fixed phrase list (the probe accepted 'please list the models').
(e) predecessorMapMention is not tied to its codebase: phoenix was accepted as PLANNED_BASELINE with langfuse's 'Langfuse OSS later'.
(f) ceiling() maps every OPEN_CONTENT outcome to DESIGN_REFERENCE_ONLY, while the definition says 'open content used as code'. A TEST_ORACLE_CANDIDATE with OPEN_CONTENT, which REUSE_OUTCOMES permits, would get DESIGN_REFERENCE_ONLY.
(g) The builder turns the roadmap's 'unknown' (agensh) and 'NONE (no licence file)' (self-harness, ophsd) into null. roadmapCheck then no longer mirrors the roadmap literally, and null means both 'repository not found' and 'no licence'.
(h) VeriHarness's SEED_STATUS says 'technical report', but its p.1 carries no such label (HERMES, JAZ and Agensh print theirs), and it leaves out the 1 Oct 2026 date that the other statuses carry.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optional: widen the TLD and '~/' patterns; bind each map mention to its codebase id; give ceiling() the reuse mode, or reword the definition; keep the roadmap's literal licence strings or document the null; align the VeriHarness status with p.1.

dispositions.evidence: The seed statuses now come from SEED_STATUS (venue, version and date only). I checked all eight against the PDFs' p.1 arXiv stamps, and the ICLR footnote for MASS: they agree. The citation names, the dataset handle and the Agensh surname are gone (SCRUB, DATASET_URL). The short names are 'Agent scaling' and 'Evolution evaluation'. My scan of crosswalk.json and README.md found no author names: none from the 108 seed-paper authors, none from the RS-CLAUDE Part A author column, and none of the 632 surnames from the PDFs' reference lists (only common words matched). It also found no e-mail or obfuscated e-mail forms, no 'corresponding author', 'et al' or affiliation/funding text, no home paths and no huggingface.co paths. The HYGIENE rule rejects the e-mail, 'et al', 'corresponding author', home-path and dataset-path probes and personal data in a dict key. Remaining pattern limits are in R2-3 (a)-(c).

CE-3 now reads 'under the fixed Gemini executor only one of four lineages (Opus, +2.70) improves held-out and the other three regress, down to -10.32'. This agrees with HarnessDev Table 6 (p.12) and pp.11 and 13 (re-read in round 1). The README row is regenerated.

Each claim now has a kind. The counts per kind match the claims: SYNTHESIS_CLAIM 45/4/0, AVAILABILITY_CHECK 4/0/6, VENUE_CHECK 1/0/0. All six NOT_FOUND rows are availability checks, and the checker rejects NOT_FOUND on a synthesis claim. The 60 claim texts compared with the grounding records: 20 identical, 17 with only the numbering removed, 23 rewritten (CLAIM_TEXT). Statuses, pages and statusDetails are unchanged. 22 of the 23 rewrites keep the meaning; VeriHarness check 9 now asserts a licence it does not have (R2-1). Numbering prefixes and the listed residue phrases are rejected by the checker. The README seed table shows the kinds.

The UPSTREAM_TEXT overrides restate the outcome and point to the open items: llm-as-a-verifier caveat to OI-2, agensh caveat to OI-4, harnessdev caveat to OI-3, the jaz 'what' to OI-1, and the veriharness 'what' to OI-7. OI-7 covers the rollout dataset licence and is carried to MAS-RA-001 and MAS-RA-002. OI-5 now ends 'recorded in the roadmap'. No 'MAS-RA-000' deferral and no 'handoff' remains in codebase texts or open items.

classify() now covers DENIED, PLANNED_UNRESOLVED, OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW, OPEN_CONTENT, ALLOWED_EXCEPTION_EXPRESSION and DEFAULT_ALLOWED in the policy's precedence; a missing licence maps to DENY_MISSING_LICENSE and anything else to DENY_UNKNOWN_LICENSE. I compared the lists with legal/third-party-license-policy.yaml 0.3.0. Probes: GPL-3.0-only labelled OPTIONAL_EXPLICIT_REVIEW and LICENSE_BLOCKED is accepted, while the DENY_UNKNOWN label is rejected; 'Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' as ALLOWED_EXCEPTION_EXPRESSION is accepted; an unknown licence and Elastic-2.0 (DENIED) are both accepted as LICENSE_BLOCKED.

The new definitions cover reuse modes, alignment, licence ceiling, policy outcomes, claim kinds, claim status and secondary naming. licenceCeiling replaces designReferenceOnly, and REUSE_OUTCOMES enforces both directions. Probes rejected: TEST_ORACLE_CANDIDATE with a missing or denied licence, NOT_APPLICABLE or NOT_RETRIEVABLE on a repository that was found, REFERENCE_DESIGN with NOASSERTION, VENDOR_CANDIDATE with NOASSERTION, and empty or 7-character map mentions. Remaining: the copied LICENSE_BLOCKED definition contradicts four records (R2-2), and map mentions are not tied to their codebase (R2-3 e).

The optional items were taken:
- MCP maps to H9 and H11 and to MAS-RA-008, and its role cites MAS-RA-008.
- RLM maps to H10 and H8, and AggAgent to H16 and H10. The derived mappings for H8, H10 and H11 follow, and the checker recomputes them.
- All 11 secondary names equal RS-CLAUDE Part A row labels (checked by script), and their sourceInputs are unchanged.
- claudes-c-compiler has a licenseNote.
- definitions.claimStatus states the rubric.
The roadmap note about the deliverables describing an in-place amendment is deferred to the owner's roadmap edit at adoption, which is acceptable.
